headline: Leakage-controlled benchmarks expose inflated accuracy in biomolecular ML models
label: Benchmark Rigor In Biomolecular Ml
summary: Random splits and redundant datasets inflate reported performance, prompting leakage-aware benchmarks for structure, binding, and kinetics models.
synthesis: Dominant thread: how dataset construction and evaluation protocols shape reported performance of ML models for biomolecular prediction. Two items directly quantify leakage. A venom ion-channel study shows random splits inflate classifier accuracy through phylogenetic leakage, and MutaStruct introduces deduplicated, leakage-aware splits for single-mutation structural change. POISK adds a patent-derived antibody-antigen set to test whether six structure prediction models discriminate binders from decoys. Other items address data scarcity and decoy sensitivity: semi-supervised kcat prediction exploits unlabeled enzyme-substrate pairs, augmentation probes protein language models trained on small complex datasets, and LangAAI shows antigen sequence context improves CDR recovery. The novelty lies in pairing modeling advances with explicit controls for leakage and decoy effects.
